coverage_limits: The arXiv API returned frequent HTTP 429 and 503 errors (shared rate limit), so after 24 API queries the remaining searches used the arXiv advanced-search web interface and full monthly listings; the web search date filter applies to the latest version, so it also surfaced older papers revised in 2026 (reported with their original first-posted date). Monthly listings for cs.AI and cs.CL (about 2,000-6,500 entries per month) were screened by title with keyword filters, so papers in those categories with nonstandard titles and abstracts outside the API and web-search vocabulary may be missed. Screening used titles and abstracts only; sample sizes, random assignment and outcome definitions were often not stated and are left null or flagged in the evidence. Primary categories outside the lane (e.g., cs.LG, physics.soc-ph, q-bio.NC) were covered only when cross-listed to a lane category or matched by the web search. Many records are AI-vs-human output comparisons, observational corpus studies, or theory and model-only homogeneity papers included for recall; screeners should apply the stated exclusions. Four records are already-collected works reported only because their arXiv records list published versions.

candidates.title: Prompt Adaptation as a Dynamic Complement in Generative AI Systems
candidates.task: prompting text-to-image models before and after a model upgrade (including an open-ended creative task)
candidates.evidence: Two preregistered experiments with 3,750 participants who wrote nearly 37,000 prompts for generative models of different capability; in the open-ended creative task, performance gains from a model upgrade came mainly from model capability rather than users' prompt adaptation. Compares AI configurations; the outcome in the creative task is rated output quality. First posted July 2024; the version found is a January 2026 revision.

candidates.title: The shrinking landscape of linguistic diversity in the age of large language models
candidates.task: writing across seven datasets (over 880,000 texts) before and after LLM rewriting
candidates.evidence: Already in the collection (Sourati et al. 2026); reported because the arXiv record (revised August 2026) lists the published version in Nature Human Behaviour with DOI 10.1038/s41562-026-02550-0. Three studies link LLM writing assistance to declines in linguistic diversity, with LLM rewriting cutting writing-complexity variance by 21-50 percent.

candidates.title: Imitating AI agents increase diversity in homogeneous information environments but can reduce it in heterogeneous ones
candidates.task: simulation of AI agents imitating Danish digital news (2022 corpus)
candidates.evidence: Large-scale simulation in which LLM agents imitate articles from the full 2022 population of Danish digital news; AI imitation increases semantic diversity in initially homogeneous environments but can reduce it in heterogeneous ones, mostly through stylistic differentiation. Simulation grounded in a real human corpus, no participants. First posted March 2025; revised February 2026.

candidates.title: Collaborating with AI Agents: Field Experiments on Teamwork, Productivity, and Performance
candidates.task: producing ads for a think tank in human-human vs. human-AI teams
candidates.evidence: Randomly assigned 2,234 participants to human-human or human-AI-agent teams that produced 11,024 ads, evaluated by independent raters and a field experiment on X; human-AI teams produced more ads per worker and higher text quality but lower image quality, and their outputs were more homogeneous (self-similar). First posted March 2025; the version found is a February 2026 revision.

candidates.title: Poor Alignment and Steerability of Large Language Models: Evidence from College Admission Essays
candidates.task: college admission essays: 30,000 applicants vs. LLM-generated essays
candidates.evidence: Compares lexical and sentence variation in essays by 30,000 applicants to a selective university with LLM-generated essays prompted with the essay question alone or with applicant demographics; LLM essays are linguistically distinct from human essays and more similar to each other, and demographic prompting does not reduce homogenization. First posted March 2025; the version found is a January 2026 revision.

candidates.title: Diverse AI personas can mitigate the homogenization effect in human-AI collaborative ideation
candidates.venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans, vol. 8, art. 100289
candidates.task: short story writing with plots from diverse AI personas (extension of Doshi and Hauser)
candidates.evidence: Already in the collection (Wan 2026); reported because the arXiv record (revised March 2026) lists the published version in Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans (DOI 10.1016/j.chbah.2026.100289). Participants wrote stories with or without plots from 10 diverse AI personas; diverse AI inputs preserved story diversity relative to a human-only baseline.

candidates.title: Augmenting Research Ideation with Data: An Empirical Investigation in Social Science
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2505.21396 (arXiv comment: AI4Science Workshop at Neurips 2025 (Spotlight))
candidates.task: social-science research ideation on climate negotiation topics
candidates.evidence: Mainly evaluates data-augmented LLM idea generation, but also reports a human study in which researchers proposed research ideas with or without LLM-generated ideas and automated validation; ideas proposed with this support were rated higher in quality. Sample size and assignment not stated in the abstract. First posted May 2025; revised February 2026.

candidates.title: IdeaBlocks: Expressing and Reusing Divergent Intents for Graphic Design Exploration using Generative AI
candidates.task: graphic design exploration with a generative-AI tool (designers)
candidates.evidence: Comparative study (N = 12) of a generative-AI design tool that lets users express and reuse divergent exploration intents against a baseline generative interface; with the tool, participants explored 2.13 times more images with 12.5 percent greater visual diversity. Compares AI configurations; also a formative study (N = 7) and a deployment (N = 6). First posted July 2025; the version found is a 2026 revision.

candidates.title: The Basic B*** Effect: The Use of LLM-based Agents Reduces the Distinctiveness and Diversity of People's Choices
candidates.task: everyday choices (e.g., movies, social media content) delegated to LLM agents
candidates.evidence: A field study of 110,000 real choices by 1,000 users and an online experiment with 348 participants compare choices made by generic or personalized LLM agents with people's own choices; agents shift choices toward popular options, reducing interpersonal distinctiveness, and personalized agents narrow the diversity of each person's choices. Outcome is diversity of choices rather than creative output; first posted September 2025, revised August 2026.

candidates.title: LLMs Homogenize Values in Constructive Arguments on Value-Laden Topics
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, pp. 1-19
candidates.task: constructive comments on homophobic and Islamophobic threads (India and US)
candidates.evidence: Experiments with 465 participants who wrote comments and reviewed human-written and LLM-rewritten constructive versions; LLM rewriting systematically diminished conservative values and elevated benevolence and universalism, a homogenization of values in rewritten arguments. Published at CHI 2026 per the arXiv record; first posted September 2025.

candidates.title: Readers Prefer Outputs of AI Trained on Copyrighted Books over Expert Human Writers
candidates.task: emulating award-winning authors' styles: MFA-trained writers vs. ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
candidates.evidence: Preregistered study comparing excerpts by MFA-trained writers with excerpts from three frontier models (in-context prompting and fine-tuning on authors' works) emulating 50 authors; in blind pairwise judgments by 28 MFA-trained and 516 general readers, prompted AI was disfavored by expert readers, while fine-tuned AI was preferred by both groups for fidelity and quality. Related to the same team's CHI 2026 paper (arXiv 2601.18353). Number of writers not stated in this abstract.

candidates.title: Personalized AI Scaffolds Synergistic Multi-Turn Collaboration in Creative Work
candidates.task: marketing campaign for a fictional startup with an LLM assistant
candidates.evidence: Randomized 331 participants to work with a generic (n = 116), partially personalized (n = 114) or fully personalized (n = 101) LLM assistant; participants with personalized AI produced marketing campaigns rated significantly higher in quality and creativity. Compares AI configurations, not AI vs. no AI. First posted October 2025; the version found is an April 2026 revision.

candidates.title: Introducing AI to an Online Petition Platform Changed Outputs but not Outcomes
candidates.task: petitions on Change.org (in-platform write-with-AI tool)
candidates.evidence: Natural experiment with difference-in-differences on 1.5 million Change.org petitions around the introduction of an in-platform write-with-AI tool; AI access changed petition lexical features and increased petition homogeneity but did not improve petition outcomes, confirmed among repeat writers before and after the tool. First posted November 2025; the version found is a September 2026 revision.

candidates.title: Stable Diffusion Models Reveal a Persisting Human–AI Gap in Visual Creativity
candidates.venue: Advanced Science, vol. 13, no. 27, art. e24142
candidates.task: visual creativity: images by visual artists, non-artists and Stable Diffusion
candidates.evidence: Compares images produced by visual artists, non-artists and a Stable Diffusion model under two prompting conditions (high vs. low human input); 255 human raters and GPT-4o scored creativity, revealing a gradient with artists highest, then non-artists, then human-inspired and self-guided AI. n counts the raters; the arXiv record lists the published version in Advanced Science (2026).

candidates.title: Writing in Symbiosis: Mapping Human Creative Agency in the AI Era
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2512.13697 (arXiv comment: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025))
candidates.task: longitudinal creative-writing corpus spanning the pre- and post-LLM eras
candidates.evidence: Analyzes a large longitudinal corpus of creative writing before and after LLMs and finds thematic convergence around AI-related topics alongside structured stylistic differentiation: some authors move toward AI style, some away, and some stay stable. Observational evidence on homogenization of human creative writing; the arXiv comment lists NeurIPS 2025. First posted December 2025; revised February 2026.

candidates.title: Exploration vs. Fixation: Scaffolding Divergent and Convergent Thinking for Human-AI Co-Creation with Generative Models
candidates.task: poster image creation with a generative co-creation system vs. ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study (N = 24) comparing a co-creation system that separates divergent exploration and convergent refinement modes with ChatGPT on a poster image creation task; the system outperformed ChatGPT on multiple creativity dimensions. Compares AI configurations. First posted December 2025; the version found is an April 2026 revision.

candidates.title: When LLM Essays Outscore Student Essays: What a Korean Writing Rubric Rewards and Where Readers Disagree
candidates.task: Korean school essays: six student essays vs. 24 LLM essays scored on a 16-criterion rubric
candidates.evidence: Secondary audit of a Korean writing study in which three raters scored six student essays and 24 essays from four LLMs on a 16-criterion rubric; LLM essays outscored student essays by 18.35 points overall, mostly on orthography and register, while student essays were highest or tied on both creativity criteria. Very small AI-vs-human comparison; n counts the raters.

candidates.title: The rise of large language models and the direction and impact of US federal research funding
candidates.authors: Qian, Wen, Furnas, Bai, Shao, Wang
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, vol. 123, no. 33, art. e2601439123
candidates.task: NSF and NIH proposals and awards
candidates.evidence: Already in the collection (Qian et al. 2026); reported because the arXiv record (revised July 2026) lists the published version in PNAS 123(33) e2601439123 (DOI 10.1073/pnas.2601439123). Higher LLM involvement in proposals is associated with lower semantic distinctiveness relative to recently funded work.

candidates.title: Do readers prefer AI-generated Italian short stories?
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2601.17363 (arXiv comment: 8 pages, peer-reviewed and accepted for presentation at New Trends in Translation and Interpreting Technology (NeTTIT 2026), paged-up for publication)
candidates.task: Italian short stories: ChatGPT-4o vs. Alberto Moravia
candidates.evidence: In a blind setup, 20 readers rated two short stories written with ChatGPT-4o and one by Alberto Moravia; the AI stories received slightly higher average ratings and were preferred more often, with modest differences. Small blind comparison of AI and human creative writing; n counts the readers.

candidates.title: Reflexa: Uncovering How LLM-Supported Reflection Scaffolding Reshapes Creativity in Creative Coding
candidates.task: creative coding with an LLM reflection-scaffolding tool
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study (N = 18) of an LLM-based reflection scaffold for creative coding; structured reflection patterns mediated the link between AI interaction and creative outcomes, broadening exploration and improving originality and aesthetic quality. The comparison condition and who rated originality are not specified in the abstract.

candidates.title: Can Good Writing Be Generative? Expert-Level AI Writing Emerges through Fine-Tuning on High-Quality Books
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2601.18353 (arXiv comment: Proceedings of CHI 2026 Conference (To Appear))
candidates.task: emulating the styles of 50 acclaimed authors: MFA writers vs. LLMs
candidates.evidence: Behavioral experiment in which 28 MFA writers competed with three LLMs to emulate 50 critically acclaimed authors; in blind pairwise comparisons by 28 expert and 131 lay judges, experts preferred human writing in 82.7 percent of cases under in-context prompting, but preferred AI 62 percent of the time after fine-tuning on the authors' works. n counts the writers; no writer used AI. CHI 2026 per the arXiv record.

candidates.title: Argument Rarity-based Originality Assessment for AI-Assisted Writing
candidates.task: argumentative student essays vs. AI-generated essays (originality as rarity)
candidates.evidence: Proposes an originality metric based on rarity within a reference corpus and applies it to 1,375 human essays and 1,000 AI-generated essays on two topics; AI essays score near-perfect on quality but their claim rarity is about one-fifth of the human level. AI output vs. human output; no participants.

candidates.title: Are Semantic Networks Associated with Idea Originality in Artificial Creativity? A Comparison with Human Agents
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, pp. 1-18
candidates.task: standardized creativity and semantic-network tests: ChatGPT-4o vs. psychology students
candidates.evidence: Administers standardized tests to ChatGPT-4o and 81 psychology students split into higher- and lower-creative groups; the expected link between semantic-network structure and originality holds when comparing ChatGPT-4o with higher-creative humans, and ChatGPT-4o is more original than lower-creative humans despite a more rigid network. CHI 2026 per the arXiv record; no person receives AI help.

candidates.title: Beyond Input–Output: Rethinking Creativity through Design-by-Analogy in Human–AI Collaboration
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, pp. 1-20
candidates.task: systematic review of design-by-analogy in human-AI creative work
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of 85 studies on design-by-analogy across the creative process, framed as a way to counter design fixation and homogenization of creative content in human-AI collaboration; classifies representations and techniques rather than pooling effects. CHI 2026 per the arXiv record. Included as a synthesis touching fixation and homogenization; it is not an effects meta-analysis.

candidates.title: Human-AI Synergy Supports Collective Creative Search
candidates.task: collective word-guessing task (human-only, AI-only and hybrid groups)
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment on collective creative search in which players guess a hidden word while seeing the best previous guess; compares human-only, AI-only and hybrid human-AI groups on performance and diversity of guesses, finding that hybrid groups perform best while preserving high diversity. Number of participants and assignment method not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Can LLMs Cook Jamaican Couscous? A Study of Cultural Novelty in Recipe Generation
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.10964 (arXiv comment: 14 pages, 12 figures, conference)
candidates.task: cross-cultural recipe adaptation (GlobalFusion country pairs)
candidates.evidence: Generates culturally adapted recipes with several LLMs for the same country pairs as a dataset of human recipe adaptations; unlike human adaptations, the divergence of LLM recipes does not track cultural distance, and models inflate novelty while failing to ground adaptations in culturally salient ingredients. AI output vs. human output on a creative cultural task; no participants.

candidates.title: LLMs Exhibit Significantly Lower Uncertainty in Creative Writing Than Professional Writers
candidates.task: story continuations by 28 LLMs vs. human-authored stories
candidates.evidence: Information-theoretic comparison showing that human-authored stories consistently have higher uncertainty than continuations generated by 28 LLMs, with larger gaps for instruction-tuned and reasoning models and in creative than functional writing; the gap correlates with writing quality. AI output vs. human output.

candidates.title: Examining and Addressing Barriers to Diversity in LLM-Generated Ideas
candidates.task: idea generation: diversity of LLM samples vs. independent human samples
candidates.evidence: Four studies show that ideas from independent LLM samples are less diverse than ideas from independent humans, attribute this to LLM fixation and to the absence of knowledge partitioning, and show that chain-of-thought prompting plus ordinary personas raise LLM idea diversity above the human level. AI output vs. human output; sample sizes not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: What Does AI Do for Cultural Interpretation? A Randomized Experiment on Close Reading Poems with Exposure to AI Interpretation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, pp. 1-18
candidates.task: close reading of poems with or without AI interpretations
candidates.evidence: Preregistered randomized experiment (n = 400) comparing no AI help with exposure to a single or multiple AI interpretations while close-reading poems; a single AI interpretation raised interpretive performance and pleasure, multiple interpretations raised performance only, and heavy reliance traded pleasure for performance. Outcome is interpretive performance, not a creativity score; included for recall. CHI 2026 per the arXiv record.

candidates.title: NarrativeLoom: Enhancing Creative Storytelling through Multi-Persona Collaborative Improvisation
candidates.task: story co-writing with a multi-persona AI system
candidates.evidence: Controlled study with 50 participants comparing stories co-authored with a multi-persona AI storytelling system against a comparison condition; experts rated the system's stories significantly higher on all Torrance dimensions (fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration), and novices benefited more. Comparison condition and assignment details are not given in the abstract.

candidates.title: How LLMs Distort Our Written Language
candidates.task: essay writing with LLMs; LLM revision of pre-2021 human essays; AI-generated peer reviews
candidates.evidence: A user study of essay writing finds that heavy LLM use raised the share of essays that stay neutral on the question by nearly 70 percent, and heavy users reported less creative writing that was less in their voice; LLM revisions of pre-LLM human essays alter meaning even under grammar-only instructions, and LLM-generated peer reviews weight criteria differently. Assignment in the user study is not described in the abstract.

candidates.title: Assessing the Effect of Cross-Domain Mapping on Creativity in Humans and Large Language Models
candidates.task: product design ideas from random cross-domain sources vs. unmet needs
candidates.evidence: Human participants and seven LLMs designed products either from a random inspiration source or from an unmet user need; LLMs produced more original ideas than humans, humans reliably benefited from cross-domain mapping while most LLMs did not, and more distant pairings raised originality in both. Compares AI and human creative output under the same intervention; no person receives AI help; human sample size not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Does AI Homogenize Student Thinking? A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Structural Convergence in AI-Augmented Essays
candidates.task: student essays: human-only, AI-only and three human+AI prompting strategies
candidates.evidence: Analyzes 6,875 essays across five conditions (human-only, AI-only and three human+AI prompt strategies) and reports a quality-homogenization trade-off: AI augmentation raised quality while cohesion structure lost 70-78 percent of its variance, perspective plurality diversified, and specific prompting reversed homogenization on argument depth. The abstract does not say whether the human+AI essays were written by participants using AI or produced by applying AI to human essays.

candidates.title: Research Novelty in Information Systems Journals After ChatGPT: Differences Across Institutional Language Contexts
candidates.task: articles in 44 top Information Systems journals, 2020-2025
candidates.evidence: Measures each article's semantic distance from its nearest recent predecessors for 13,847 articles; after ChatGPT, articles from first authors at institutions in non-English-dominant countries show a 0.176 SD larger decline in relative semantic novelty. The authors note individual LLM use is not observed, so this is a post-2022 shift rather than an adoption effect. First posted March 2026; revised July 2026.

candidates.title: Beyond Via: Analysis and Estimation of the Impact of Large Language Models in Academic Papers
candidates.task: word usage in arXiv titles and abstracts
candidates.evidence: Documents LLM-driven shifts in word usage in arXiv papers (e.g., more "beyond" and "via" in titles, fewer "the" and "of" in abstracts) and estimates heterogeneous, changing real-world LLM usage. Outcome is lexical uptake rather than diversity or creativity; included as context alongside excess-vocabulary studies.

candidates.title: Voice-based debate with an AI adversary is associated with increased divergent ideation
candidates.task: open-ended debates between university students and an AI adversary (voice vs. text)
candidates.evidence: Analyzes 957 open-ended debates between students and a knowledgeable AI adversary; spoken interactions were more verbose and repetitive but explored a wider range of ideas than text-based ones, suggesting that apparent homogenizing effects of AI partly reflect the text medium. Outcome is breadth of ideas expressed; how modality was assigned is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Human Thinking under Plural LLM Assistance: Mathematical Problem Solving and Open-Ended Writing
candidates.task: open-ended essay writing (and math problem solving) with single vs. plural LLM assistants
candidates.evidence: Two controlled experiments with 562 participants in total; in the writing task, participants wrote with no LLM, a single generalist assistant, or two role-specialized assistants; LLM help improved essay quality, and the role-specialized pair preserved more idea diversity than the single assistant. The math experiment also measures unassisted post-task performance. Random assignment is not stated in the abstract; first posted April 2026, revised July 2026.

candidates.title: The Ideation Bottleneck: Decomposing the Quality Gap Between AI-Generated and Human Economics Research
candidates.task: economics research papers: AI-generated (APE project) vs. AER and AEJ papers
candidates.evidence: Compares 912 AI-generated economics papers with 41 human papers published in top journals, using model-based scores for idea quality and execution; the idea-quality gap (d = 2.23) is larger than the execution gap (d = 0.90) and accounts for about 71 percent of the quality difference. Research ideation by AI vs. humans; no participants; scores come from model-based raters.

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.task: creative writing with an interactive AI assistant under different incentives
candidates.evidence: Preregistered randomized controlled trial in which participants could use AI interactively in a creative writing task; those rewarded for originality relative to peers produced collectively more diverse writing than those rewarded for quality alone, mainly by incorporating fewer AI suggestions verbatim. All arms have AI access; the manipulation is the incentive. Sample size not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: POEMetric: The Last Stanza of Humanity
candidates.venue: ICLR 2026 (as listed in the arXiv record)
candidates.task: poems in seven fixed forms: 203 human poems vs. 6,090 poems from 30 LLMs
candidates.evidence: Evaluates human poems and LLM poems written to the same forms and themes on instruction following, creativity, lexical diversity, idiosyncrasy, emotional resonance and imagery, using rule-based scores and LLM judges validated by human experts; human poets scored higher on creativity, idiosyncrasy and overall quality. AI output vs. human output; ICLR 2026 per the arXiv record.

candidates.title: Strategic Algorithmic Monoculture: Experimental Evidence from Coordination Games
candidates.task: coordination games played by human and LLM subjects
candidates.evidence: Experimental design separating baseline action similarity from incentive-driven similarity, run on human and LLM subjects; LLMs show high baseline similarity (algorithmic monoculture) and, unlike humans, struggle to sustain heterogeneity when divergence is rewarded. Non-creative task; included as context on AI-vs-human diversity of choices. Human sample size not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Measuring Creativity in the Age of Generative AI: Distinguishing Human and AI-Generated Creative Performance in Hiring and Talent Systems
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.19799 (arXiv comment: Research Paper Presented at the this http URL @MIT Conference, April 2, 2026)
candidates.task: measuring creativity as novelty in synthesis for hiring and talent assessment
candidates.evidence: Proposes embedding-based metrics for creativity as novelty in idea generation and transformation and reports an empirical evaluation suggesting a shift toward bimodal distributions of creative output in AI-mediated environments. The abstract does not describe the data or whether AI use was observed; included for recall as a measurement paper with an AI-related distributional claim.

candidates.title: From Searchable to Non-Searchable: Generative AI and Information Diversity in Online Information Seeking
candidates.task: real-world ChatGPT conversations vs. Google search results (information seeking)
candidates.evidence: Uses over 200,000 real ChatGPT interactions: most queries are non-searchable and span a broader knowledge space, but for comparable searchable queries AI responses are less diverse than Google results, and the diversity of AI responses predicts later changes in the diversity of users' inquiries. Outcome is diversity of information and of user queries, not creative output; included as context.

candidates.title: NexusAI: Enabling Design Space Exploration of Ideas through Cognitive Abstraction and Functional Decomposition
candidates.task: design ideation with an LLM tool that decomposes and recombines ideas
candidates.evidence: Within-subject user study (N = 14) comparing an LLM-based diagramming system that decomposes, abstracts and recombines generated ideas against a baseline; the system improved design space exploration, reduced cognitive overhead and helped reframing, which the authors read as mitigating fixation. Compares AI configurations.

candidates.title: From Planning to Revision: How AI Writing Support at Different Stages Alters Ownership
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Designing Interactive Systems Conference, pp. 2903-2934
candidates.task: short essay writing with AI support at the planning, drafting or revising stage
candidates.evidence: Already in the collection (Gero 2026); reported because the arXiv record lists the DIS 2026 proceedings version (DOI 10.1145/3800645.3813003). Between-subjects study (n = 253): AI drafting support contributed the most ideas and reduced ownership most, while more AI contributions improved essay quality.

candidates.title: Temporal Flattening in LLM-Generated Text: Comparing Human and LLM Writing Trajectories
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.12097 (arXiv comment: 25 pages, 6 figures. To appear in Findings of ACL 2026)
candidates.task: longitudinal writing (abstracts, blogs, news) by 412 human authors vs. LLM-generated trajectories
candidates.evidence: Compares 6,086 documents by 412 human authors over 2012-2024 with trajectories generated by three LLMs; LLM text shows greater lexical diversity but much less semantic and cognitive-emotional drift over time (temporal flattening). AI output vs. human output; n counts the human authors whose existing texts were analyzed. Findings of ACL 2026 per the arXiv record.

candidates.title: Creo: From One-Shot Image Generation to Progressive, Co-Creative Ideation
candidates.authors: De Simone, Boggust, Durand, Wilson, Satyanarayan
candidates.task: image creation with a multi-stage text-to-image system vs. one-shot generation
candidates.evidence: Comparative study of a multi-stage text-to-image system (rough sketch to high resolution, with editable intermediate stages) against a one-shot baseline; participants felt stronger ownership, and embedding-based analysis shows the multi-stage outputs were less homogeneous than one-shot results. Sample size and assignment not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Impact of large language models on peer review opinions from a fine-grained perspective: Evidence from top conference proceedings in AI
candidates.task: peer review reports at top AI conferences before and after LLMs
candidates.evidence: Examines fine-grained changes in peer review reports after LLMs emerged, estimating which reviews are LLM-modified; reviews became longer, more fluent and more standardized in language, with more focus on summaries and surface clarity and less on originality and critical reasoning. Observational evidence of standardization of human-written evaluative text; the arXiv comment lists Scientometrics.

candidates.title: Measuring and Mitigating Persona Distortions from AI Writing Assistance
candidates.task: political opinion paragraphs written with and without AI assistance
candidates.evidence: Three large experiments in which 2,939 writers wrote opinion paragraphs with and without AI assistance and 11,091 blind readers rated them on 29 dimensions; AI assistance made writers seem more opinionated, competent and positive and shifted their perceived demographics toward more privileged groups, a systematic distortion of expressed persona. Outcome is reader-perceived persona rather than creativity; random assignment is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Directional Alignment and Narrative Agency in Human-LLM Co-Writing
candidates.task: turn-based human-LLM co-written stories (corpus of 87 stories)
candidates.evidence: Applies sentiment and semantic-novelty modeling to a corpus of 87 human-LLM co-written stories; human turns introduce more semantic novelty and steer later developments, while LLM turns mostly elaborate and adapt emotionally. No comparison without AI; companion to the authors' later human-human vs. human-LLM study (arXiv 2609.07920).

candidates.title: When and How AI Should Assist Brainstorming for AI Impact Assessment
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency, pp. 2745-2780
candidates.task: team brainstorming for AI impact assessment (in-person workshops)
candidates.evidence: After co-design workshops (28 participants), ten in-person workshops with 54 participants evaluated AI interventions for structured team brainstorming; AI improved impact-assessment quality and brainstorming perceptions for a chatbot-companion use case but not for a specialized kidney-allocation application. FAccT 2026 per the arXiv record; comparison and assignment details not given in the abstract.

candidates.title: More Aligned, Less Diverse? Analyzing the Grammar and Lexicon of Two Generations of LLMs
candidates.authors: Gude, Santos-Ríos, Bond, Flickinger, Gómez-Rodríguez, Zamaraeva
candidates.task: English news text: two generations of LLMs vs. New York Times articles
candidates.evidence: Uses HPSG grammar parsing and ecological diversity metrics to compare syntactic and lexical diversity of news text generated by older and newer LLMs with human-authored New York Times articles from two years; newer instruction-tuned models show reduced syntactic and especially lexical diversity, while human news text changed little. AI output vs. human output; no participants.

candidates.title: Human-AI Co-Evolution and Epistemic Collapse: A Dynamical Systems Perspective
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.06347 (arXiv comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, ICML EIML Workshop submitted)
candidates.task: theory of human-AI co-evolution and diversity of knowledge
candidates.evidence: Short workshop paper with a three-variable dynamical model (human cognition, data quality, model capability) whose simulations show that rising reliance on AI can push the human-AI loop toward a low-diversity equilibrium. Theory and simulation only, no human data; listed because comparable theory papers on homogenization are in the collection.

candidates.title: The Cost of Perfect English: Pragmatic Flattening and the Erasure of Authorial Voice in L2 Writing Supported by GenAI
candidates.task: argumentative essays by Chinese L2 university students (ICNALE), polished by LLMs
candidates.evidence: Compares original L2 student essays with versions polished by four LLMs (no student used AI); models removed dialogic engagement markers and recast authorial stance, which the authors read as homogenization toward an Anglo-American rhetorical norm. Outcome is pragmatic and stylistic diversity, not rated creativity.

candidates.title: Usable but Conventional: An Empirical Study on the UX of AI-Generated Interface Prototypes
candidates.venue: Anais do LIII Seminário Integrado de Software e Hardware (SEMISH 2026), pp. 830-841
candidates.task: user-interface prototypes made by GenAI tools vs. by humans
candidates.evidence: Survey in which 92 participants rated AI-generated and human-created interface prototypes without knowing authorship on the UEQ-S; AI prototypes scored well on pragmatic qualities but neutral or negative on hedonic qualities including originality and innovation. n counts the raters; no person received AI help.

candidates.title: Overreliance in Writing Tasks: Exploring Similarity-Based Measures of AI Influence on Writing and Proposing a Reflective Writing Interface Intervention
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency, pp. 5941-5958
candidates.task: analysis and synthesis writing tasks with or without AI suggestions
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods study in which 47 participants completed writing tasks with or without AI assistance; textual overlap between AI suggestions and participants' writing shows substantial suggestion reuse, and a follow-up think-aloud (n = 4) tests a reflective interface. Outcome is similarity of writing to AI text, a homogenization-related measure; assignment method not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Dynamics of collective creativity in AI art competitions
candidates.task: human-AI co-created images in Artbreeder remix parties
candidates.evidence: Analyzes 130,882 images from 368 Artbreeder remix parties, where users iteratively remix each other's AI-generated images from a seed; images become simpler and converge toward common thematic attractors, and users prefer to remix less novel parents even though novel parents yield more novel children. All output is AI-assisted, so there is no no-AI comparison; outcome is novelty, complexity and convergence.

candidates.title: What Are LLMs Doing to Scientific Communication? Measuring Changes in Writing Practices and Reading Experience
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Language Resources and Evaluation Conference, pp. 1811-1830
candidates.task: NLP papers in the ACL Anthology (2020-2024) and LLM-improved passages
candidates.evidence: Diachronic lexical analysis of over 37,000 ACL Anthology papers plus a synthetic set of 3,000 human passages and their LLM-improved versions; LLM-modified texts show lower lexical diversity and specific syntactic shifts, and 20 domain experts rated LLM-improved texts as more understandable. n counts the expert annotators in the pilot rating study.

candidates.title: Framing an AI with Values Reduces AI Reliance in AI-supported Writing Tasks
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency, pp. 5237-5264
candidates.task: AI-supported essay writing (Indian and American participants)
candidates.evidence: Between-subjects online experiment (n = 149) in which participants wrote with AI suggestions with no intervention, after seeing the AI's framed values, or after comparing those values with their own; seeing the AI's values cut the AI-generated share of essays by 20 percent and produced essays with more unique text. All arms use AI; the outcome on uniqueness bears on homogenization.

candidates.title: AI-Associated Lexical Shifts Across 34 Languages: Cross-Lingual Convergence and Diachronic Uptake in News Writing
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.25358 (arXiv comment: 19 pages (9-page main body, plus references and appendices), 3 figures; ACL ARR reviewed, committed to EMNLP 2026)
candidates.task: news writing in 34 languages (WMT News Crawl)
candidates.evidence: Identifies words that GPT-4.1 overuses relative to matched human text in 34 languages and tracks their prevalence in news writing before and after ChatGPT; AI-overused items rose in 26 of 34 languages (mean +15.1 percent) while baseline words did not, read as cross-lingual homogenizing pressure on language use. Outcome is lexical uptake, not creativity.

candidates.title: Elias in the Lighthouse, Again? Diagnosing Low Diversity in LLM Stories
candidates.task: short stories generated by four LLMs from five prompts
candidates.evidence: Samples 20,000 stories from four current LLMs and finds that 11 words (names such as Elias and Elara, lighthouse settings, clockmaker professions) occur in 88.3 percent of them across models; these tokens are rare in published literature and pretraining data but common in preference data. Mainly model-output homogeneity, benchmarked against human-written literature; no participants.

candidates.title: AI Research Agents Narrow Scientific Exploration
candidates.task: research ideas generated by AI research agents vs. human-authored papers
candidates.evidence: Generates 219,655 research ideas with five agent frameworks and five LLMs and compares them with human-authored papers in the same areas; AI ideas are more concentrated, stay closer to the starting literature than human follow-on work, and align less with future human research. AI output vs. human output; no person receives AI help.

candidates.title: Accommodation Goes Both Ways: Studying Linguistic Convergence Between Humans and Language Models
candidates.task: linguistic style accommodation in real ChatGPT conversations (WildChat)
candidates.evidence: Measures linguistic convergence between users and ChatGPT in a large corpus of real multi-turn conversations in eight languages; LLMs over-converge toward users, while human convergence toward the model matches human-human baselines. Outcome is stylistic accommodation of human messages, not a creativity score; included as context on AI-driven convergence of human expression.

candidates.title: Argument Collapse: LLMs Flatten Long-Form Public Debate
candidates.task: opinion essays on public debate questions (NYT debates, Boston Review forums)
candidates.evidence: Compares 1,487 human responses to debate prompts with 23,381 LLM-generated essays; 65.3 percent of human main arguments are unique within a debate versus 3.4 percent of LLM main arguments, and diversity prompting recovers only about half of the distinct human arguments. AI output vs. human output; no person receives AI help.

candidates.title: Contemporary AI lacks the imagination to diverge or negate in science
candidates.authors: Bao, Wu, Liu, Li, Cao, Evans
candidates.task: scientific idea generation; 39 million papers 2010-2025
candidates.evidence: Scientists (6,749 raters) judged LLM-generated ideas derived from their own papers; non-reasoning LLMs collapse into a narrow hivemind of similar ideas, and an analysis of 39 million papers finds that after ChatGPT's release null claims are suppressed and ideas contract. Mixes model evaluation with an observational corpus analysis; n counts the scientist raters, who judged AI ideas rather than producing ideas.

candidates.title: GraphStory: Collaborative Story Writing through Event-Based Narrative Editing
candidates.task: story writing with a graph-based AI writing system
candidates.evidence: User study with professional and semi-professional writers comparing a graph-based story ideation and generation system with a normal AI-based writing workflow; the system reduced organizing effort and better supported creativity and exploration. The abstract does not say whether creativity was rated on outputs or self-reported; included for recall.

candidates.title: CASPER in the Machine: Insights into Character Variety in LLM-Generated Stories
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.22454 (arXiv comment: Proceedings of ACL, 2026)
candidates.task: character portrayal in LLM-generated vs. recently published human-written stories
candidates.evidence: Compares characters in stories generated by popular LLMs with characters in recently published human-written stories on eight narratological dimensions, asking whether LLMs produce similar characters and a variety of characters. AI output vs. human output; no human participants.

candidates.title: Which India Survives Translation? Narrative Homogenisation Across Indian Oral Traditions in LLMs
candidates.task: storytelling in three Indian oral and literary traditions
candidates.evidence: Pilot study comparing texts generated by two LLMs with authentic reference corpora from three Indian traditions; cross-tradition similarity of LLM outputs is high relative to the genuine distance between traditions, indicating partial homogenisation. Model outputs compared with human-authored reference texts; no human participants.

candidates.title: Analyzing Students' Statistics Writing Before and After the Emergence of Large Language Models
candidates.task: undergraduate statistics data-analysis reports, 2021-2025
candidates.evidence: Corpus of over 1,600 student reports shows writing style and verb use becoming more similar to LLM style after LLMs became available, and also more similar to expert statistical writing. Outcome is stylistic similarity to LLM text rather than diversity among students or creativity; included as context.

candidates.title: Reviving Reflection-in-Action: Instilling Designerly Thinking in AI-Supported Ideation through Multimodal Prompting
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Creativity and Cognition, pp. 359-376
candidates.task: design ideation with an AI creativity support tool (design students)
candidates.evidence: Within-participants study comparing input modalities for an AI creativity support tool (text, sketch, sketch plus tags) on design students' divergent thinking; sketch input tended to raise fluency, with inconclusive differences in variety, originality and quality. Compares AI configurations, not AI vs. no AI; sample size not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Human--LLM Collaboration Is Transforming Complexity Metrics in Scientific Texts
candidates.authors: Bentley, Vidiella, Ruck, Dutta, Li, Valverde
candidates.task: arXiv abstracts, 2010-2025
candidates.evidence: Applies complexity metrics (vocabulary size, Zipf and Heaps exponents, turnover of top-ranked words) to millions of arXiv abstracts, using 2023 as a natural-experiment break; an LLM-associated style index rises sharply after early 2023, turnover among top words increases, and the link between the style index and vocabulary-based complexity flattens. Outcome is lexical diversity and complexity of scientific text.

candidates.title: Floor Raiser or Ceiling Limiter? Differential Storytelling Outcomes with a Child-Centric GenAI System Across Individual Differences
candidates.task: children's storytelling (ages 7-12)
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects experiment (N = 40, grades 2-6) comparing GenAI-assisted storytelling with a traditional storyboard condition; GenAI raised creativity and richness ratings and narrowed the quality gap between children by 83.5 percent (convergence in quality, not content). Counterbalancing is not described in the abstract.

candidates.title: AGC-Bench: Measuring Artificial General Creativity
candidates.task: creativity benchmark across 78 datasets (brainstorming, narrative, humor, STEM)
candidates.evidence: Benchmark of 83 LLMs on creativity tasks built from a systematic review of AI-creativity benchmarks; on a human-matched subset, the top human still outperforms the top LLM. Mostly model evaluation; the human comparison is the relevant context. Human sample size not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Measuring the Gap Between Human and LLM Research Ideas
candidates.task: research idea generation from prior-paper contexts
candidates.evidence: Prompts LLMs to generate research ideas from the prior works that inspired real human papers and compares the distribution of LLM ideas with the human papers on a research-taste taxonomy; LLM ideas concentrate on bridge-like opportunities and synthesis methods, a narrower range than human ideas. No person receives AI help.

candidates.title: AI Models Can Predict and Collaboratively Modulate Human Memory Search
candidates.task: semantic fluency task (memory search) with LLM support
candidates.evidence: Uses the semantic fluency task, a divergent/convergent thinking paradigm, to test whether an LLM can predict human memory-search trajectories and, per the title, collaboratively modulate them. The abstract does not state whether people were assigned to LLM help or which creativity or diversity outcome was scored; included for recall.

candidates.title: Comment on arXiv:2607.01233: Survivorship Bias in Published-Paper Baselines for Research-Idea Distributions
candidates.task: comment on human vs. LLM research-idea distributions
candidates.evidence: Two-page comment on arXiv 2607.01233 arguing that using published papers as the human baseline introduces survivorship bias, so the measured gap between human and LLM idea distributions may be overstated. No new human data; listed because it bears on interpreting an AI-vs-human diversity comparison.

candidates.title: Central Tendency Bias in Human Selection of AI-Generated Design Variations
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.09018 (arXiv comment: Accepted at the 2026 Human-AI Interaction and Experience Design (HAXD 2026) Conference)
candidates.task: selecting among AI-generated design variations
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment manipulating the variance of sets of AI-generated design variations (high vs. low) and measuring which designs participants select; higher variance increased selection of center-proximal designs, which the authors read as constrained selection diversity. Outcome is the diversity of human choices among AI outputs, not of human-made output; sample size not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Monoculture: AI Homogenizes Syntax, Not (Necessarily) Semantics
candidates.task: Kaggle competition code submissions, 2019-2026
candidates.evidence: Measures within-contest similarity of Kaggle code submissions before and after the spread of AI coding assistants, separating surface syntax (TF-IDF n-grams) from approach or intent (code embeddings); submissions became more alike in syntax but show no homogenization in approach. Single-author working paper.

candidates.title: FIERO: Empowering Creative Writing Through Collaborative Game Play
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.11837 (arXiv comment: 51pages, 14 figures, 5 tables, will be presenting this paper at CHIPLAY 2026)
candidates.task: collaborative storytelling card game with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Compares a multiplayer card game whose interface uses generative AI to synthesize ideas and generate visuals against online collaborative writing alone (N = 60); the game raised idea fluency, novelty generation and story plot coherence. The AI is bundled with physical cards and game play, and the assignment procedure is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: The One-Word Census: Answer-Choice Conformity Across 44 Language Models
candidates.task: single-word category answers (e.g., name a tree) across 44 language models
candidates.evidence: Measures answer convergence across 44 LLMs on 31 open one-word prompts; in 7 of 31 categories one answer takes over 80 percent of model answers, and against human category-production norms the models are more concentrated than people in 18 of 20 shared categories. Mostly model-only; the comparison with human norms is the relevant context.

candidates.title: HALO: Interactive Co-abductive Reasoning in Scientific Hypothesis Generation
candidates.task: molecular hypothesis generation in drug discovery (medicinal chemists)
candidates.evidence: Expert study with 10 medicinal chemists comparing a human-AI co-abduction system with a comparison condition; with the system, participants produced higher-quality and more diverse candidate molecules. Comparison condition and assignment are not detailed in the abstract.

candidates.title: Generative AI floods and dilutes the market for books
candidates.task: self-published genre fiction on Amazon, 2023-2026
candidates.evidence: Applies full-text AI detection to 14,419 self-published genre-fiction books matched to daily sales; books with substantial AI text gain sales share, and top-selling AI-text books draw on more distinctive language from existing books than books without AI text. Outcome is market dilution and textual overlap with prior books, a derivativeness measure linked to generative AI.

candidates.title: Offline-to-Online Creative Optimization with Generative Models and Adaptive Testing
candidates.task: online ad creatives (field experiments on an ad platform)
candidates.evidence: Deploys a workflow in which a generative model, guided by a predictive model trained on past A/B tests, produces ad creatives that are tested in adaptive online experiments; in a 50-arm field experiment the best generated creative had 45.1 percent higher engagement than the best human-authored creative, with similar upper-tail lifts in two more experiments. Outcome is audience engagement, not a creativity rating; no person receives AI help.

candidates.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Scientific Research: Individual Benefits, Collective Risks, and a Framework for Responsible Research with AI
candidates.task: generative AI in scientific research (roundtable and literature mapping)
candidates.evidence: Narrative review drawing on a roundtable and the recent empirical literature; concludes that AI-assisted research shows gains in publication volume and citations while evidence on novelty, disruption and breakthrough output is ambiguous or negative, and proposes a governance framework. Not a systematic review; included for recall as a synthesis touching novelty and diversity of science.

candidates.title: Linguistic Monoculture in LLM-Assisted Language Use
candidates.task: theory of LLM-assisted writing and linguistic diversity
candidates.evidence: Mathematical model in which authors and shared or personalized LLMs coevolve; shared models pull authors toward a common linguistic norm, while personalization can preserve diversity, and individually rational authors over-conform. Theory with synthetic simulations only (no human data); included because comparable theory papers on homogenization are in the collection.

candidates.title: AI and Its Impact on Creativity and Diversity: An Empirical Study of LLM-Generated Product Ideas
candidates.authors: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich
candidates.task: new product ideas for college students (under $50)
candidates.evidence: Series of eight studies comparing LLM-generated with human-generated product ideas: LLM ideas have higher average purchase-intent quality but are less novel and less diverse at the set level; also re-analyzes prior LLM creativity studies and tests diversity-restoring prompts. Appears to consolidate the authors' earlier idea-generation papers (Girotra et al. 2023; Meincke, Mollick and Terwiesch 2024), which are already collected.

candidates.title: Language Models Agree With Each Other, Not With Readers
candidates.task: choosing salient sentences in web documents (reader highlights)
candidates.evidence: Compares sentence selections by 18 LLM configurations with 2,523 organic reader highlight sets on 120 documents; models agree with each other far more than readers agree with each other, evidence of model-side convergence relative to a naturally occurring human reference. Non-creative task; included as context on homogenization measurement.

candidates.title: The Assistant Erased You: Measuring Loss of Authorship Signals in AI-Mediated Communication
candidates.task: AI rewriting of personal blogs, workplace email and news (pre-GenAI corpora)
candidates.evidence: Rewrites human-authored texts with an AI writing assistant and measures how much authorship attribution accuracy falls (Idiolect Erasure Rate); heavy rewriting cuts attribution by up to 66.5 percentage points and produces stylistic convergence across authors. Simulated AI assistance on existing human texts; no participants.

candidates.title: When AI Writes, Who Gets Cited? Evidence of Citation Monoculture Across Language Models
candidates.task: selecting papers to cite from blinded candidate panels
candidates.evidence: Eleven LLMs from three vendors select up to ten papers from random panels of thirty with masked metadata; all models concentrate citations on the same narrow subset (citation monoculture), while eight domain experts selecting from the same blinded panels show no comparable shared preference. Non-creative selection task; included as context on cross-model homogenization relative to humans. n counts the expert selectors.

candidates.title: Enacting Constructive Conflicts with AI Agents to Enhance Reconsideration among Novice Interaction Designers
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.04166 (arXiv comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, conditionally accepted to Human-Agent Interaction 2026)
candidates.task: interaction design proposal revision (design students)
candidates.evidence: Between-subjects experiment with 45 design students in three conditions: unsupported self-reflection, written stepwise guidance, or an AI agent that enacts stakeholder conflict; the AI-agent group generated and discarded more ideas and made more design improvements than self-reflection. Idea counts and design improvements are the closest creativity outcomes; random assignment is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: One Tool, One Taste? How Vibe Coding Trades Collective Diversity for Individual Creativity
candidates.task: promotional website design with a vibe-coding tool (graduate course)
candidates.evidence: Analyzes 73 websites that graduate students built with the vibe-coding tool Lovable for real businesses; image-embedding similarity and clustering show strong within-cohort visual concentration (88 percent of sites in six clusters) despite an assignment that rewarded originality. No no-AI comparison group; the number of students is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Where Models Converge and Humans Diverge: A Coverage Framework for Distributional Pluralism in Open-Ended Generation
candidates.task: ideation and narrative tasks (e.g., Harry Potter fanfiction)
candidates.evidence: Proposes coverage metrics that compare the distribution of LLM-generated content with the empirical distribution of human writing on the same topic; across ideation and narrative tasks, LLMs produce plausible but narrow content concentrated near the center of the human response space. AI output vs. human output.

candidates.title: The Algorithmic Flattening of Sound: Computational Evidence and Justice Implications of AI Music Homogenization
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.06106 (arXiv comment: To be published in AAAI/ACM AIES 2026)
candidates.task: music generation in four genres (Suno, Lyria 3)
candidates.evidence: Generates 100 tracks per system and genre and compares them with equal-sized human music corpora on 72 audio features; one system reduces within-genre acoustic diversity and the other collapses distinctions between genres. AI output vs. human output; no person receives AI help.

candidates.title: AI-AI co-creation outperforms human pairs in creative tasks
candidates.task: open-ended creative idea tasks (three tasks)
candidates.evidence: Experiment comparing ideas from AI-AI co-creation (two role setups), single-AI creation and human-human pairs across three open-ended tasks; trained judges rated 1,212 ideas on creativity, novelty and usefulness, and both AI-AI conditions beat single AI and human pairs on creativity and novelty. Humans do not receive AI help; number of human participants not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: VeriForge: Mitigating Latent Knowledge Gaps in Narrative Drafting via Mixed-Initiative Scaffolding
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.09698 (arXiv comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, Accepted by UIST'26)
candidates.task: fiction drafting with a knowledge-discovery writing system
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects user study (N = 12) of a mixed-initiative AI writing system for discovering domain knowledge while drafting fiction, compared with a baseline condition; expert raters judged passages written with the system to have stronger domain grounding, and the system supported creative exploration. Outcome is expert-rated grounding rather than a creativity score.

candidates.title: Most biomedical publications show signs of LLM-assisted writing
candidates.task: full texts of open-access biomedical papers (PubMed Central)
candidates.evidence: Estimates the share of biomedical papers with excess LLM-associated vocabulary using changing word frequencies; by the end of 2025, 89 percent of papers show such excess. Outcome is prevalence of LLM-style vocabulary rather than diversity; included as context because the earlier excess-vocabulary paper by the same group (Kobak et al.) is in the collection.

candidates.title: Surprise2Refine: Axis-Centered Exploration-To-Refinement for Agent-Assisted Creative Scaffolding
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.12605 (arXiv comment: Accepted to ACM UIST 2026)
candidates.task: design exploration with an agent-assisted creative scaffolding tool (designers)
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study with 14 designers comparing an agent-assisted tool that broadens and narrows a design space along user-defined axes with a comparison workflow; the tool improved sense of control and the perceived creativity of design outcomes. The abstract does not say whether creativity was rated by the designers themselves or by others; included for recall.

candidates.title: Novels generated by language models show compressed formal variation
candidates.task: novel-length fiction generated by LLMs vs. human novels
candidates.evidence: Contrasts novels generated repeatedly by two LLMs in two target styles with 270 human-written novels on lexical and syntactic measures; AI novels vary far less from one another in sentence structure, readability and punctuation than human novels do. AI output vs. human output.

candidates.title: Asymmetric Discourse Homogenization and Shared Language Technology: Evidence from Reddit
candidates.task: political discussion on Reddit, 2019-2025
candidates.evidence: Uses 6 million Reddit comments from two cross-partisan forums to test for a break in the diversity (semantic similarity) of political discourse around the arrival of ChatGPT; conservative users show an interrupted diversification trend, progressive users do not, and the effect vanishes among authors active throughout. The author reads the mechanism as community-level convergence rather than individual AI adoption.

candidates.title: Weaker Coherence, Weaker Reciprocity: Comparing the Semantic and Social Organization of Moltbook and Reddit
candidates.authors: Di Ciocco, Celauro, Pinto, Kuperman, Balenzuela
candidates.task: online community content: AI-agent network (Moltbook) vs. early Reddit
candidates.evidence: Compares semantic coherence and diversity of communities on a social network populated by AI agents with early Reddit; AI-agent communities are more homogeneous and less differentiated. AI-generated vs. human-generated content at platform level; included as context.

candidates.title: Navigating Epistemic Monocultures in AI-Driven Science: A Simulation Study
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.19390 (arXiv comment: Accepted at Philosophy of Science)
candidates.task: simulation of AI guidance in scientific communities (NK landscape)
candidates.evidence: Agent-based NK-landscape model of scientists guided by AI; uniform AI guidance helps only under narrow conditions and otherwise homogenizes and harms search, while personalization can preserve diversity. Simulation only, no human data (accepted at Philosophy of Science per arXiv comment); listed as theory context on homogenization.

candidates.title: Towards Cognitive Process-Aware Proactive Writing Support
candidates.task: creative writing with proactive AI writing support
candidates.evidence: Two within-subjects studies (N = 21) compare an AI co-writer that infers cognitive writing processes and offers proactive suggestions with comparison configurations; the authors report improved expressiveness and idea exploration. The comparison conditions and assignment order are not detailed in the abstract.

candidates.title: Citing Less Critically: LLMs Reshape the Rhetoric and Reach of Scientific Citation
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.01432 (arXiv comment: Accepted at the EMNLP 2026 main conference)
candidates.task: citation sentences in NLP conference papers (masked-citation task)
candidates.evidence: Has six LLMs regenerate 63,000+ masked citation contexts from 1,746 NLP papers and compares them with the human originals; LLMs cite less critically and over-cite popular and older papers. Outcome is citation intent and concentration on popular work (a narrowing of what is cited), not creativity; included as marginal context.

candidates.title: AI agents reshape consensus formation in human groups
candidates.task: collaborative description (convention-formation) game in mixed human-AI groups
candidates.evidence: Experiment varying the proportion of LLM agents in human groups that form shared naming conventions through repeated pairwise communication; high agent shares produce strong, agent-led and more abstract consensus, and humans gradually adopt agent expressions. Outcome is convergence of expressions (homogenization), not creativity ratings; number of human participants not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: How LLMs Build Fictional Worlds: Setting and Narrative Space in AI-Generated Creative Storytelling
candidates.task: fiction worldbuilding (setting), English and German
candidates.evidence: Compares 1,000 stories per model from four LLMs with human-authored Project Gutenberg fiction on the distribution of narrative-space types; LLMs systematically overproduce perceived space relative to the human baseline. Outcome is a stylistic feature of setting, not a creativity rating, so relevance is context only.

candidates.title: Collective creativity in hybrid societies
candidates.task: perspective on collective creativity with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Narrative perspective/review (not systematic) arguing that AI-assisted ideation raises individual novelty while narrowing population-level diversity and that the mix of humans and models in hybrid collectives decides the outcome. Included for recall as a synthesis of the homogenization literature; it reports no new data.

candidates.title: LLM Signals in Funded Grants: Evidence from International Funding Agencies
candidates.task: funded grant abstracts (NSF, NIH, UKRI), 2017 to mid-2026
candidates.evidence: Brief report tracking LLM-overproduced words and phrases in 221,425 funded grant abstracts before and after ChatGPT's release. Outcome is uptake of LLM-style vocabulary in grant writing rather than diversity or novelty; included as context next to the collected work on LLMs and research funding.

candidates.title: An LLM-Associated Register Shift in Korean Journal Abstracts: A Morphology-Aware Excess-Vocabulary Study, 2018-2026
candidates.task: Korean journal abstracts (KCI), 2018 to August 2026
candidates.evidence: Adapts the excess-vocabulary method to Korean using 398,296 abstracts; LLM-associated words rise from late 2024 (e.g., one marker in 21.4 percent of 2026 abstracts vs. 5.3 percent expected), with bounds on the share of LLM-processed abstracts. Outcome is uptake of LLM-style register, not diversity or creativity; included as context alongside the collected excess-vocabulary work.

candidates.title: Humans Introduce, Models Elaborate: Asymmetric Narrative Agency in Human-LLM Co-Writing
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.07920 (arXiv comment: 12 pages, 11 figures, EMNLP 2026)
candidates.task: turn-based collaborative storytelling (human-human, human-LLM, LLM-LLM)
candidates.evidence: Compares matched turn-based storytelling conditions with a human partner, an LLM partner, or two LLMs, using turn-level measures of semantic novelty, transience and resonance; in human-LLM pairs humans introduce more novel and persistent material while the LLM elaborates. Outcome is computed novelty of contributions; assignment and sample size not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: More than half of recent astronomy papers are written with language-model assistance
candidates.task: full texts of astro-ph papers, 2015 to mid-2026
candidates.evidence: Hierarchical Bayesian model of LLM-marker word counts in 207,111 astronomy papers estimates that more than half of 2025 papers were written with language-model assistance, while under 1 percent disclose it. Outcome is prevalence of LLM-style vocabulary, not diversity or originality; included as context alongside the excess-vocabulary literature.

candidates.title: AI Use Conditions and Perspective Diversity in Ethical Decision-Making: A Pilot Study of Human Reasoning Processes
candidates.task: ethical dilemma reasoning (business case)
candidates.evidence: Pilot experiment with 29 participants in AI-prohibited, AI-optional or AI-mandatory conditions; blind coders scored perspective diversity and counterargument diversity of responses. The AI-mandatory group considered a broader range of perspectives (significant on the perspective index), while final conclusions converged across conditions. Assignment method not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Calibrated Ambiguity in Multimodal Language Models: Humans reach for cultural references, while models describe the picture
candidates.task: Dixit-style picture clues (calibrated ambiguity)
candidates.evidence: Compares clues for Dixit picture cards written by humans and by multimodal language models, coded with a rubric for calibrated ambiguity; model clues are over-specified (ambiguity collapse) and almost never draw on culturally situated references, unlike human clues. Creative-language task; no person receives AI help; human sample size not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Generative AI and Extended Reality in Collaborative Architectural Design Education: An Exploratory Studio Study
candidates.task: collaborative architectural conceptual design studio (undergraduate)
candidates.evidence: Classroom study in which four of seven self-selected student teams (27 students) used a GenAI plus extended-reality pipeline for ideation and three did not; a seven-member panel rated team design presentations, with no significant difference between conditions. Outcome is panel-rated presentation quality rather than an explicit creativity score.

candidates.title: "Looking for Something Weird to Happen": How Humans Sustain AI Agent Novelty Amid Semantic Collapse
candidates.authors: Lai, Woemmel, Mao, Kim, Ann, Evans
candidates.task: human-configured AI agents on an agent social network (Moltbook)
candidates.evidence: Tracks 30,076 active AI agents that human users configure and steer; agent output becomes less diverse within agents and more similar across agents over weeks, while a minority of agents sustains high novelty. Interviews (N = 11) and a survey (N = 53) of users link sustained novelty to users who value novelty and supply broad, distinctive material. Output is AI-generated under human steering, so this is context on semantic collapse rather than assisted human creativity.

candidates.title: Spook the Machine: Gamified Exploration of Human Imagination of Machine Fear
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.15472 (arXiv comment: To appear in the Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Affective Computing and Intelligent Interaction (ACII 2026))
candidates.task: generating images to frighten AI agents (public online game)
candidates.evidence: Public deployment in which 832 participants created 15,719 generated images in a 2x2 design varying the AI agents' emotional expressiveness and whether rewards counted novelty; rewarding novelty sustained collective creative diversity, while without it users repeated earlier successes; expressiveness did not change creative output. All participants use generative tools; the manipulation is the AI agent and reward design, not AI help vs. none.

candidates.title: Integrating Flipped Learning and Generative AI for Practice-Based Design Education: Evidence from a Knit Yarn Design Course
candidates.task: knit yarn design course (undergraduate)
candidates.evidence: Course-based comparison of a historical control cohort (N = 12) with an intervention cohort (N = 16) that used flipped learning plus a GenAI-assisted visual ideation module; the intervention cohort scored higher on creativity thinking and design skills. The AI component is bundled with flipped learning, and the authors call the evidence exploratory, not causal.

candidates.title: Converging Naming Styles, Persistent Network Locality: GitHub in the LLM Era
candidates.task: identifier naming styles in public GitHub repositories, 2015-2025
candidates.evidence: Characterizes naming styles in GitHub repositories across six languages; repositories with detected LLM-related commits use longer identifiers and more already-prevalent patterns, and naming-style diversity of new cohorts drops around 2023-2024, while network-local variation persists. Observational link between LLM tools and convergence of a creative-convention outcome.

candidates.title: AI-written admissions essays are widespread but penalized
candidates.task: admissions essays for a public policy master's program, 2020-2025
candidates.evidence: Analyzes about 7,500 applications and uses the abrupt arrival of ChatGPT to estimate effects of AI availability: most 2025 applicants submitted at least one primarily AI-generated essay, AI availability raised essay writing quality, and AI-written essays were admitted less often; an experiment with admissions officers shows they rate suspected AI essays lower. Outcome is writing quality and admission rather than creativity or diversity; included next to the collected admissions-essay studies.

candidates.title: How Did Writing Change At CHI? Analyzing 44 Years of CHI Writing Before and After the Introduction of Large Language Models
candidates.task: CHI conference papers, 1982-2026
candidates.evidence: Analyzes full texts of 14,262 CHI papers for readability, register, lexical diversity and LLM marker words before and after LLMs; prose did not homogenize and vocabulary grew more varied, though LLMs accelerated a pre-existing word-level shift.

candidates.title: Small-world Networks of Agents Brainstorm AI Risks to Support Ideation
candidates.task: participatory AI risk ideation (Futures Wheel sessions)
candidates.evidence: Eleven teams of young chatbot users ideated AI risks starting either from a risk list written by 45 AI practitioners (control) or from a list generated by an LLM agent-network framework (treatment); treatment teams identified more risks and more systemic risks. The paper also rates the novelty of the framework's own risk lists versus single-LLM brainstorming; team assignment method and number of people not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: AI-Generated Email Drafts Shift Culturally Distinctive Communication Styles in Professional Email
candidates.task: workplace email writing by Japanese and American participants
candidates.evidence: Preregistered within-subject experiment in which participants wrote emails without AI, with a low-context AI draft, and with a high-context AI draft; AI drafts pulled participants' emails toward the draft's cultural style, most when the draft was culturally misaligned. Outcome is cultural style markers (homogenization of communication norms); sample size and order randomization not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Improving Today, Narrowing Tomorrow: Collective Learning, Diversity, and Generativity
candidates.task: theory of collective learning and diversity among firms (relevant to generative AI)
candidates.evidence: Agent-based model of firms searching interdependent landscapes in which learning from a common repertoire improves current performance but can narrow future variety; copying leaders consumes diversity, while repertoires combined with local judgment preserve it. Theory and simulation only, framed around generative AI; no human data.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligences and human scientists exhibit complementary strengths in theory building
candidates.task: social-science theory building (gender and race inequality)
candidates.evidence: Compares theories, predictions and revisions produced by 25 LLMs with those of 13 senior researchers and 60 doctoral scholars (no person receives AI help); blinded raters scored AI theories higher in quality, while human theories were more diverse and gained more from aggregation. n counts the 73 human scientists only.

candidates.title: More of the same? Are scientific papers losing originality?
candidates.task: full-text scientific papers in eight fields, 2015-2025
candidates.evidence: Screens more than 26,000 full-text papers for passages that resemble recent literature; the share of text resembling recent work was stable before 2021 and more than tripled by 2025, with a parallel rise in passages expressing the same scientific idea. The abstract measures originality as textual distinctness and does not attribute the rise to generative AI directly; included because the timing coincides with LLM diffusion.

candidates.title: Scanvas: Discovering and Developing Synergistic Opportunities in Generative Design Spaces
candidates.task: design concept generation (professional designers)
candidates.evidence: User study with 12 professional designers comparing an AI system that searches for synergistic design opportunities against LLM ideation baselines; users produced significantly higher-quality, more synergistic concepts with the system. Compares AI configurations; assignment details not given in the abstract.

candidates.title: Investigating Human--AI Discrepancies via Multiple-Solution Problems
candidates.task: multiple-solution reasoning puzzles (270 puzzles, five families)
candidates.evidence: Compares the distribution over valid solutions chosen by people and by frontier models on puzzles with 3 to 8 correct answers; models resemble each other far more than they resemble humans, and model distributions are less diverse than human ones in every puzzle family. Non-creative task; included as context on AI-vs-human diversity of choices. Human sample size not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Correctness, Convergence, and AI-Generated Code Detection: A Longitudinal Study of Student and Large Language Model Code in Introductory Programming
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2610.00863 (arXiv comment: accepted at Koli Calling '26)
candidates.task: student code submissions in introductory Python labs (2021, 2023, 2025)
candidates.evidence: Compares 29,970 student submissions across three cohorts with 90,000 LLM-generated solutions; later cohorts match LLM references more often, and on tightly specified functions the number of distinct student code forms declined across cohorts, while open-ended functions stayed diverse. Cohort comparison before and after LLM availability; outcome is diversity of student solutions.
